query: Microsoft FY2024 Q3 earnings capital expenditure data center AI spending
normalized: ai capital center data earnings expenditure fy2024 microsoft q3 spending

output.content:
Microsoft’s FY2024 Q3 (quarter ended March 31, 2024) capital expenditure—including finance leases—was **$14.0 billion**, explicitly directed to cloud demand and scaling AI infrastructure; cash paid for property, plant and equipment was **$11.0 billion**. [[1]] 

This represented a **$2.5 billion, or 21.7%, sequential increase** from FY2024 Q2’s $11.5 billion capex including finance leases; cash PP&E spending increased $1.3 billion, or 13.4%, from $9.7 billion. [[2]] [[1]] 

Management characterized near-term AI demand as slightly above available capacity, said it was continuing to bring capacity online, and guided for capex to rise **materially sequentially in FY2024 Q4**, driven by cloud and AI infrastructure investment. [[1]] 

The spending was occurring alongside strong cloud demand: Azure and other cloud-services revenue grew **31% year over year**, with AI services contributing **7 percentage points** to that growth, while Intelligent Cloud revenue rose **21%** to **$26.7 billion**. [[1]] 

Microsoft also said FY2025 capex would exceed FY2024 capex, subject to demand and adoption signals, indicating that the Q3 buildout was part of a continuing data-center and AI-capacity expansion rather than a one-quarter surge. [[1]]

sources.title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2024 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call
